clue.text: Outstanding performer, kind to imitate

blocks.note: a class is a kind or category
to act is to pretend or imitate

explanation.surface: A star performer who is generous enough for others to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A class act is an idiom for someone of conspicuous quality, especially a top entertainer.

clue.text: A hat, something for the gardener outdoors?

blocks.note: first meaning: a close-fitting bell-shaped woman's hat
second meaning: a glass or plastic cover put over young plants

explanation.walkthrough: The French word for bell names both shapes; the question mark hints that the gardener's item is not worn.
explanation.definitionFit: The bell-shaped word covers both a 1920s hat and the protective cover a gardener sets over seedlings.

clue.text: Painter displaying unusual traits

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of the next word are not in their ordinary order

blocks.note: the letters of traits, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter with an eccentric personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is one kind of artist, a person who makes works of art.

clue.text: Track about boy with female, romantically attached

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for a track goes round the other pieces

blocks.note: spoor is the track or trail of an animal
a boy's name
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A young man is tracked with his girlfriend: they are clearly an item.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spoken for is already in a relationship, an idiom for being romantically taken.

clue.text: What may arrive in the post from Manx chap, in character

definitions.text: What may arrive in the post

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word that follows loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written before docking
taken as written
a character of the alphabet is a letter

explanation.surface: A postcard from a man on the Isle of Man, written in his own idiom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' looks like a place clue for the Isle of Man, but it works like the tailless Manx cat, docking the word chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain letter is mailed to several people, each asked to copy and send it on.

clue.text: Cavalryman caught in country road close to Sedgemoor

indicators.note: something caught in a thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow country road
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the last letter of Sedgemoor

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier stopped on a lane near Sedgemoor, scene of the 1685 battle in Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught; it sits inside the word for a country road, and the R from Sedgemoor follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer is a mounted soldier armed with a lance, so a type of cavalry soldier.

clue.text: Military commander, elected once more

blocks.note: an aga was an Ottoman military commander
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A general is returned to office for another term.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means one more time, a straight synonym for once more.

clue.text: Chinese-style dish, food had by me at home

blocks.note: chow is slang for food
taken as written
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A takeaway eaten in the speaker's own house.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a stir-fried noodle dish served in Chinese restaurants.

clue.text: Make another appraisal concerning fools on top of statue

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
asses are fools
the first letter of statue

explanation.surface: An art critic rethinks after fools are found climbing on a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate something again, the same as making another appraisal.

clue.text: Left to choice in platoon, I suspect

indicators.note: as an adjective suspect means dodgy or not right, so the letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: the letters of platoon plus I

explanation.surface: A soldier guesses that attendance in the platoon is not compulsory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is not required, so it is left to one's own choice.

clue.text: Temple of a deity in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so the state abbreviation wraps the rest

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
taken as written
a deity is a god

explanation.surface: A shrine to some god found somewhere in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in Asia.

clue.text: Urgency shown by the man crossing a street

indicators.note: someone crossing a road straddles it, so this piece spans either side of the other

blocks.note: the man is referred to as he
taken as written
ST is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A man dashes across the road in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurried speed, the quality of acting with urgency.

clue.text: Awfully mean celebrities - say who they are

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the word that follows is jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of mean, to be rearranged
celebrities are big names

explanation.surface: A spiteful gossip is urged to identify the famous people involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To name names is an idiom for identifying people, especially those implicated in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Teacher resents planners

blocks.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
someone who minds something objects to or resents it

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher bears a grudge against those who organise things.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterminds are the people who plan and direct a complex scheme.

clue.text: Mavericks may make no charge for gins, vodkas, etc.

blocks.note: something with no charge is free
gin and vodka are examples of spirits, distilled drinks

explanation.surface: Rebels might offer drinks at the bar on the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Free spirits are independent, unconventional people, as are mavericks who go their own way.

clue.text: Join unfortunate gent coming in hopping mad

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters of the next word are disordered
something coming in enters another, so it sits inside the word for angry

blocks.note: someone hopping mad is irate, very angry
the letters of gent, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A furious man barges in and is asked to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine things so they unite, as join can mean.

clue.text: A racket rising, rising in slaughterhouse

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going upwards, so the next word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a racket is a bat for tennis or squash
a rising is an uprising, a riot

explanation.surface: Noise and rioting break out in an abattoir.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word does two jobs: the first 'rising' signals the reversal, the second is a noun for a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a slaughterhouse, the French-derived term for a place where animals are killed for meat.

clue.text: Hoax the French about time for game

indicators.note: about means around, so the French article goes around the abbreviation

blocks.note: a skit is a send-up or spoof
les is French for the (plural)
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: French players pulling a prank at the moment for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles is a game of knocking down wooden pins with a ball, an old British pub game.

clue.text: London home of detective in song?

blocks.note: first meaning: the street where Sherlock Holmes lived at 221B
second meaning: Gerry Rafferty's 1978 hit with its famous saxophone riff

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is the title of a particular song rather than a description.
explanation.definitionFit: The street address of Conan Doyle's fictional sleuth is also the title of a well-known pop record.

clue.text: Caddy initially glued broken club

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the word before are reassembled

blocks.note: the first letter of caddy
the letters of glued, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A golf caddy has stuck a snapped golf club back together.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing scene makes 'club' look like a golf club; it is a heavy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short thick stick used as a weapon, a type of club.

clue.text: A doctor tucking into mother's curry

indicators.note: someone tucking into a meal goes inside it, so these pieces enter the word for mother's

blocks.note: Ma is mother, so mother's is Ma's
taken as written
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A GP eating a home-cooked curry made by Mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A madras is a fairly hot curry named after the Indian city now called Chennai.

clue.text: Four-letter word used by girl upset about closure of restaurant

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over or turned upside down, so the girl's name runs backwards
about means around, so the name goes round the other piece
the closure of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a girl's name
the final letter of restaurant

explanation.surface: A girl storms out of a restaurant at closing time, swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name must be found from the answer's letters: MARGARET reversed is TERAGRAM, and T goes after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is literally a group of four letters, so any word of four letters qualifies.

clue.text: Sign of tooth decay, canine needing to be extracted

indicators.note: extracting a tooth removes it, so this letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: caries is the dental term for tooth decay
C stands for canine in dental charts

explanation.surface: A dentist spots signs of decay and decides a canine must come out.
explanation.walkthrough: The dental scene makes 'Sign' look like a symptom; it is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Cheese made by pair back in Georgia

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the word for a pair is read backwards
one thing in another is enclosed by it, so the state abbreviation wraps the rest

blocks.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia
a pair of performers is a duo

explanation.surface: A couple returning home to Georgia make cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild Dutch cheese named after the town where it was traded.

clue.text: Grease gear in drilling installation

blocks.note: to grease something is to oil it
rig means equipment or gear

explanation.surface: An instruction to lubricate the machinery on a drilling platform.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is the structure, often offshore, that holds the equipment for drilling oil wells.

clue.text: Aim to provoke compromise

blocks.note: an end is an aim or goal
to anger someone is to provoke them

explanation.surface: Advice on negotiating: set out to annoy and then settle halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compromise' reads as a noun for meeting halfway, but it is the verb meaning to put at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety or security is to expose it to danger, which is what endanger means.

clue.text: Endure sister, drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of sister, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put up with their intoxicated sister.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to withstand or hold out against pressure, which is a sense of endure.

clue.text: Along with a very fashionable person, meets a head of state

indicators.note: the head of a word is its beginning, so only its first letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
a swell is an old word for a smart, fashionable person
taken as written
the first letter of state

explanation.surface: A fashionable socialite is introduced to a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a president, but only the initial S is used.
explanation.definitionFit: As well as is a phrase meaning in addition to, which is what along with means.
